implementation_notes: The provider owns delivery: after setMessageListener() the JMS implementation invokes onMessage on its own thread whenever a message arrives, and the application never calls receive(). The javadoc pins down two constraints that shape production code - an exception thrown from onMessage is a client programming error, and setMessageListener must not be used inside Java EE web/EJB components, where a message-driven bean or container-managed listener must own delivery. Choose this form for standalone clients, custom containers, or when provider session semantics (transacted sessions, selectors) are the point.
pitfalls: An exception thrown from onMessage is a client programming error - the provider may swallow it or drop the listener; convert failures to rollback/nack/dead-letter inside the callback.
A JMS Session is not thread-safe and its listener is called serially; sharing the session with other threads breaks the provider's contract.
setMessageListener is forbidden in Java EE web/EJB components (the javadoc warns it may throw JMSException there) - the container must own delivery.
Auto-acknowledge plus a crash mid-callback loses the message unless the session is transacted or the client acknowledges after the work.

variants.name: Spring message-driven POJO (@JmsListener / DefaultMessageListenerContainer)
variants.idiom_name: @JmsListener on a POJO method; container owns delivery
variants.implementation_notes: Spring turns the endpoint into a plain method: @JmsListener marks it, and a message-listener container owns sessions, concurrency, reconnection, transactions and redelivery while translating the checked JMSException hierarchy into unchecked exceptions. This is the idiomatic choice in Spring applications because the listener stays a testable POJO and delivery policy is declarative configuration; the raw setMessageListener form remains for standalone clients or custom containers.
pitfalls: The container decides concurrency ("3-10" above); listener beans must be thread-safe or the concurrency pinned to 1.
Listener exceptions follow the container's error handler - the default rolls back and redelivers, so configure an ErrorHandler/back-off and a dead-letter path.
